hypothesis: Output truncation keeps a smaller head, a larger tail (test summaries, last traceback) and error-like lines from the omitted middle, with the cap lowered 30k to 20k chars; the same signal in fewer tokens per long output. Mainly a token saver; unsure it moves the score. Prediction is a low-confidence guess: a task with long Go test logs where the failing line may sit in the omitted middle.
targets_mode: spec_clause_not_exercised_in_own_checks (failing lines of long test runs must not be lost); token cost
why_not_lower_lever: A cut in the wrong place is a tool behavior; no instruction can restore text the tool dropped.
trigger_condition: A tool output longer than 20000 characters.
retroactive_check: corrective: none predicted by task; preservative: short outputs are untouched and the tail (where summaries sit) gets more room than before; transfer: any repo with long build or test logs.
regression_risk: Outputs between 20k and 30k chars now lose some middle text that was shown before.

Acts during the work, unlike earlier end-of-run reminders; unsure, effect may be inside noise.
why_not_lower_lever: No checkable moment exists for a hook: which clauses matter and where is semantic; guidance has to be present while the pieces are built, so the system prompt is the place.
trigger_condition: Always present in the system prompt; applies when the request states error behavior, flags or ambiguous points.
